title: A solute lowers the freezing point and raises the boiling point
caption: Dissolving a non-volatile solute lowers the solvent's vapour pressure, shifting the liquid–gas line down (boiling point up) and the solid–liquid line left (freezing point down). For 1 mol of NaCl in 1 kg of water (2 mol of ions) ΔTb = 1.02 K and ΔTf = 3.72 K. Not to scale.
alt: The phase diagram of water with the solution's boundaries dashed: the liquid region widens at both ends.
description: Dashed lines: the solution. Its liquid–gas line lies lower and to the right, its solid–liquid line to the left.
So the solution boils above 100 °C and freezes below 0 °C.
